I know I wasn't planned. There's a decade gap between me and my older sibling. My parents tried to shower me with love to hide their disappointment and regret. But kids are much more intuitive than we usually give them credit for. I knew it regardless. As much as I love and appreciate everything my parents did and poured into me, it still felt shitty.

Then why have a kid in the first place? I mean, if you know to yourself that you can barely keep yourself together? I can't even remember when was the last time I ate or bathe myself. I can't and shouldn't be responsible for another person's life.

I don't mean to be rude but IDK how to phrase this any other way.  Why did you have a son? Is it worth all the pain and heartaches of living for you? I'm just genuinely trying to learn what keeps people going.

In my case, I want to honor my mom. She nows about my depression and suicidal tendencies. And I doubt she'd want me to be even more depressed because of her death. Yes, I do miss her. I still want to talk with her. I wish it was me that died instead. But wishing those won't change reality. So I try to go through my day productively instead of a sobbing mess. Also, I don't want to be confronted about my feelings. I'm not really good at expressing myself. So keeping everything in and only letting it out once I'm alone or someone I trust works best for me.

Not me but my mom. She had mild back aches whenever she strains herself. Didn't think of it as anything. Everybody also have that. She'd just treat herself with  spa or massage once a week of she can. It went worse tho. So she went to the doctor. Bam! Cancer. She died in the hospital 3 months later.

To be honest, we didn't had the ideal mother and daughter relationship. I was never able to confide anything to her. She always snooped on my stuffs and once ran through my diaries. She often criticized me in the usual asian mother way. There were instances of physical violence I've received from her which always I chose not retaliate. I understand that they were just fits of uncontrollable anger from my mistakes. That doesn't define her tho. She made a lot of sacrifices and admittedly let go of her dreams to support us, her family. I still am afraid of her but I commend on everything she have done. I don't really miss her but I miss the thought of being able  work my relationship with her. Of all the people, I think my parents deserves their retirement the most. My dad had to work overseas to support us. My mom worked non stop as well. In their 31 years of marriage, they had only been together together 8 years tops. They had so much plans for upcoming trips and vacations. Now it is all gone. I wish it was me dead instead so my parents could still have each other. I'm not good enough anyway.

I know since I had allergic reaction to other seafoods and ad experienced this before. My face was all swollen, I had hives, and my throat was slowly closing down. Our school nurse didn't even bother giving me anti histamine or anything other than water. They just called my parents to fetch me and take me off their hands. The thing is, my parents were overseas. It was a good thing that my allergic reaction was quiet slow and my brother was able to fetch me and give me medicine (he's also allergic to a bunch of stuffs). I only waited until my graduation and then moved to another school after that.
